transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Maya Rivera (Hawthorne Procurement), Ethan Cole (Hawthorne CISO), Lena Park (Hawthorne Legal), Devon Hayes (Hawthorne Eng)

Summary: procurement focused call to close MSA/DPA open items, confirm SLA options and pricing for Dedicated capacity, and schedule a technical benchmark pilot to validate latency/throughput. Transcript contains some transcription noise and occasional mis-heard product names.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya and Samir are with me. Maya, Ethan, Lena, Devon — thanks for taking time. Quick agenda: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA options and pricing, and next steps for a pilot.

[00:35] Maya: Thanks Jordan. We want to make sure timeline looks doable — procurement is targeting vendor sign-off by mid-Oct. Main blockers are DPA retention language and SLA guarantees.

[01:05] Jordan: Understood. Priya, do you want to run through the SLA tiers and Dedicated pricing?

[01:12] Priya: Sure. So we have Hosted API standard, and Redwood Dedicated which is reserved GPU pools. For SLAs we can offer 99.9% uptime on Dedicated with a latency SLO target per route; there's also a premium SLA (99.95) that includes faster failover and a small price bump. We've put together a pricing worksheet — I'll share after the call.

[01:55] Ethan: Quick Q — for Dedicated, what does data isolation look like? We need customer-owned keys and audit logs. KMS and HSM support?

[02:15] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports customer KMS integration — we support AWS KMS and bring-your-own-HSM options in Private deployments. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available via Redwood Console; note sometimes the transcript shows Console as "Redwood Consolel" in our docs, haha.

[02:45] Lena: On the DPA, we have two main asks: 1) retention windows no longer than 30 days for requests and 2) contract language around termination and data deletion within 14 days.

[03:10] Jordan: We can accept a 30-day retention for customer request data on Hosted; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-controlled retention and can configure immediate purge on termination. We'll need to capture exact language for the DPA redline.

[03:45] Devon: From engineering perspective, we want to run a benchmark with our actual prompt mix — mostly long-form generation and embeddings for search. Will Redwood support KV cache warmup and continuous batching to mimic production?

[04:05] Priya: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache, continuous batching, quantization profiles. We'll set up a benchmark with a fixed dataset; note that kernels and compilation can change throughput based on sequence length. Also worth mentioning that internal comments sometimes transcribe KV cache as "K-V cash" so ignore odd spellings.

[05:00] Maya: On SLAs, what's the credits model? We need clear remedies for missed SLOs and a limit on liability.

[05:20] Jordan: Standard is service credits proportional to downtime; we can surface exact formula in the SLA exhibit. For liability we have carrier-backed limits and can discuss enterprise add-ons for higher liability caps. Lena, that aligns with typical market terms?

[05:45] Lena: We'll need to confirm with legal. Also please include SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation in the security pack. We already asked for that but haven't received the latest report.

[06:05] Samir: We'll send the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts after the call — plus our security questionnaire and a short security deck for your procurement team.

[06:25] Ethan: Are there any data residency constraints? We operate in EU and US, want certain PII kept in EU.

[06:40] Priya: We support region-specific routing and can pin workloads to EU regions on Hosted or Dedicated in that region. For Private we can deploy in your VPC on-prem. There may be slight latency differences but we can quantify in the benchmark.

[07:15] Devon: Regarding authentication, do you support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC for team access?

[07:30] Jordan: Yes SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported, and Redwood Console supports role-based access controls. We'll include an RBAC matrix in the onboarding docs.

[08:00] Maya: Can we talk pricing structure — commit vs pay-as-you-go? Procurement prefers a reserved capacity commit for predictability but need to see the pricing tiers.

[08:20] Priya: Dedicated is reserved with monthly/annual commits; we can do a blended model for the pilot. I'll include burst capacity options and how autoscaling works.

[09:00] Lena: On termination language — standard 30-day notice and data deletion timeline — can Redwood accept a 14-day deletion obligation? Jordan, you said 14 earlier for Dedicated?

[09:18] Jordan: For Dedicated with customer-controlled keys we can commit to 14-day deletion and provide deletion certificates. For Hosted, the 30-day retention is more standard unless we add stricter terms in the DPA.

[10:00] Ethan: Security review question — does Redwood support customer-managed keys with rotation schedules and HSM import? We have strict KMS requirements.

[10:20] Priya: Yes, AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS supported; BYO-HSM supported in Private. Rotation schedules are honored, and we surface key IDs in audit logs. We'll share the cryptography FAQ doc.

[11:05] Devon: For the benchmark, can Priya's team mock our production concurrency distribution? We'll need to simulate mixed short/long sequences and embedding bursts.

[11:20] Priya: Absolutely. If you share sample prompt traces and target p95 latency, we'll reproduce. Suggest a 2-hour window where we run samples on Dedicated and Hosted variants. That will help with cost/latency tradeoff.

[12:05] Maya: Timeline — procurement wants to sign MSA by Oct 15. Is that realistic?

[12:20] Jordan: Yes, if legal redlines are exchanged this week and we have a legal follow-up next week we can make that milestone. We'll commit to sending a redline today or tomorrow.

[12:45] Lena: We'll review the redline and revert within 3 business days if possible. Also cc the counsel handling vendor obligations.

[13:10] Jordan: Noted. Competitors — are you evaluating other vendors?

[13:20] Maya: We're also looking at Anthropic for chat and OpenAI for some prototyping, and our infra team is keeping an eye on internal GPU stack economics.

[13:45] Jordan: Good to know. We'll highlight predictable unit economics and Dedicated SLAs.

[14:05] Ethan: A quick question on monitoring: can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?

[14:25] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-model and per-route breakdown, tracing, and alerting. We'll provide screenshots in the onboarding packet.

[15:10] Devon: Any friction with model version pinning for rollouts? We need stable outputs for production.

[15:25] Priya: You can pin model versions and use rollout policies — canary and A/B. We also have eval hooks to detect quality regressions tied to your prompt set.

[16:05] Maya: For pricing approval I need an itemized worksheet for budget committee — include committed vs overage pricing and pilot discounts.

[16:20] Priya: We'll include an itemized worksheet and an example cost scenario based on your estimated token usage.

[17:00] Lena: One more legal — indemnity and export control clauses, we'll send specifics but please flag anything unusual.

[17:15] Jordan: Sounds good; we'll have legal review the MSA redline and flag export control language.

[17:40] Samir: Action items recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO, pricing worksheet, redlined MSA, and schedule the benchmark.

[18:05] Maya: Thanks — can we meet next Tuesday for legal follow-up?

[18:15] Jordan: Yes, propose Oct 6 14:00 UTC — we'll send an invite.

[18:40] Devon: One last note — for the benchmark we'd like to test both quantized and non-quantized model paths to understand quality vs cost.

[19:00] Priya: Agreed — we'll include quantization profiles in the benchmark plan.

[19:30] Lena: OK, thanks everyone. We'll look for the docs and redline.

[19:45] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the package after the call.

End transcript. (Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings of product names, e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "red wood dedicated" in some snippets.)
